root.name: Sicilian Defense: Velimirovic Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nf6 5. Nc3 d6 6. Bc4 e6 7. Be3 Be7 8. Qe2

overview: In the Sozin set-up White plays Be3, Qe2 and 0-0-0, then pushes g4-g5 or f4 and Rhg1 for a kingside attack. Black castles and counters on the queenside with ...Qc7, ...a6, ...Na5 and ...b5. It leads to opposite-side castling and sharp, theory-heavy play where one slip loses quickly.

white_ideas.idea: Castle long, then play Rhg1 and g4-g5 or f4-f5
Use Nd5 or Bb3 and Nxc6 to exploit the open d-file

typical_structures.structure: Open d-file, White pawns e4/f2/g2/h2, Black pawns d6/e6

character.notes: Mutual attacks on opposite wings with a race.

structure.notes: Half-open c-file for Black, d-file after the exchange.

character.reason: Opposite-side castling and mutual attacks make it a race.

soundness.reason: The line is well tested for both sides.

structure.reason: Like every Sicilian the c-file is half open for Black.

approach.reason: A main-line anti-Najdorf set-up that strong players use.

level.reason: Long forcing lines that must be known, with hard plans.

plans.reason: The two kings are on opposite sides and each camp attacks.
